physics_goals.quote: A Broadband/Resonant Approach to Cosmic Axion Detection with an Amplifying B-field Ring Apparatus.
physics_goals.value: Search for axion dark matter over a broad mass range using a lumped-element (non-cavity) toroidal magnetometer technique

summary.plain: ABRACADABRA-10 cm was a small prototype at MIT that searched for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, using a toroidal magnet instead of the resonant cavities other experiments use. Its axion search finished around 2021.
summary.technical: Small-scale (10 cm) lumped-element/broadband toroidal-magnetometer axion haloscope prototype at MIT; 1-month first run (2018) and a final broadband run (published 2021) set world-leading limits at sub-ueV axion masses before the dedicated axion-search program concluded.

unique_capabilities.quote: we probe the hypothesis that axions constitute dark matter, using the ABRACADABRA-10cm experiment in a broadband configuration, with world-leading sensitivity
unique_capabilities.value: First lumped-element (broadband, non-resonant-cavity) axion haloscope to publish limits, demonstrating the technique for future large-scale detectors
